rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the full retention window without being excessively steep or slow. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early, elute in the hold, or are missing, guiding the next narrowing and slope adjustments.

All 10 peaks eluted well within the gradient, so trim the solvent window to the actual elution region to improve efficiency and reduce time while keeping selectivity similar. This should test whether a narrower, better-targeted window can maintain full resolution and cut the time penalty.

The broad window was clearly better, so now test a steeper version to reduce run time while probing whether the critical mid-cluster loses much resolution with slope. Comparing this directly to injection 1 will show how slope-sensitive the closest pairs are.

The critical mid-cluster is strongly slope-sensitive: halving tG caused the 5–7 region to collapse, while 20 min was fully resolved but slower. An intermediate tG should recover enough resolution for the worst pair while keeping the run short and potentially improving CRF over both previous broad-window runs.

The optimum appears to lie between 14 and 20 min on the broad window, with the (6,7) pair controlling CRF. A small increase from 14 to 16 min should improve that pair’s resolution with only a modest time increase, making it a strong candidate to beat the current best.

Since 14 min is near-optimal for time but the (6,7) pair is still limiting, test temperature as the remaining lever for selectivity. A modest drop to 35 C may improve that close pair’s spacing without adding enough retention to incur a time penalty.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity in the critical cluster, so probe the opposite direction. A small increase to 45 C may shift the close-pair selectivity favorably while keeping the near-optimal 14 min broad gradient and likely preserving zero time penalty.

Temperature moves made the critical cluster worse, so keep 40 C and instead test a slightly lower phi1 to narrow the gradient window without the severe slowdown seen at phi1 0.65. This may modestly flatten the effective slope in the mid-elution region and improve the limiting pair while staying in the no-time-penalty regime.

The slight reduction of phi1 improved CRF, so continue narrowing the upper end cautiously to see if the critical mid-cluster gains a bit more resolution without pushing the last peak too late. This is a focused local refinement around the current best method.

At phi1 0.90 and tG 14 min the method is close to ideal, with only the (6,7) pair slightly limiting and no time penalty. Testing a slightly steeper gradient checks whether we can keep that pair near the current resolution while gaining a small robustness or score advantage from a shorter run.

The local optimum looks near phi1 0.90, and the 12 min test confirmed the critical pair is still slope-sensitive. A 16 min run at the current best phi window should reveal whether slightly more slope relief can raise the resolution term to 1.000 with only a small or no time penalty.

The best region is clearly phi1 0.90 and tG 14 min, so the remaining opportunity is a different temperature near the optimum. Since 35 C and 45 C were both worse, test 30 C to see if selectivity shifts nonlinearly enough to improve the critical cluster while still keeping the run in the zero time-penalty zone.

Temperature has a strong, nonmonotonic effect on selectivity, so after poor results at 30, 35, and 45 C it is worth checking 50 C as the last nearby temperature option around the best phi-window/slope. This could still improve the limiting pair through a different reordering/selectivity shift while likely keeping runtime short.

The best method remains tightly localized at 40 C, but temperature effects are clearly irregular, so 25 C is the last untested extreme that could in principle create a favorable selectivity shift. It is a worthwhile final temperature screen at the best gradient settings before focusing the remaining budget on fine phi-window optimization.

Temperature exploration is exhausted, so return to the best region and test the lower edge of the phi window. Raising phi0 slightly may reposition the early/mid compounds within the gradient and alter the critical cluster’s selectivity without a large runtime penalty.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved the best method, so continue in the same direction with a small additional increase while keeping the successful upper limit and slope. This should show whether the critical mid-cluster benefits further from being shifted to a slightly lower effective gradient range.

The current best came from increasing phi0, while a lower phi1 was also slightly favorable earlier, so combine both improvements in one focused test. This may further tune the effective gradient window around the critical cluster while keeping all peaks within a short, penalty-free run.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so use the remaining budget to map nearby conditions around the optimum and confirm robustness. Increasing phi0 slightly while keeping the winning phi1 may reveal whether the optimum is broad or sharply peaked without risking truncation.

With two neighboring methods now at the maximum score, continue defining the high-scoring plateau by lowering phi1 one more step from the winning condition. This checks how far the upper bound can be reduced before time penalty or selectivity loss appears.

Lowering phi1 too far introduced time penalty, so keep phi1 at the proven optimum 0.85 and probe the upper side of phi0 once more. This maps whether the 1.000 plateau extends to a still higher starting composition and helps identify the most robust final method.

Now that the optimal phi window is established, test whether a slightly steeper gradient can still retain a perfect CRF within that window. This defines how much slope tolerance the optimum has and whether the same selectivity can be achieved in an even shorter run.

A 12 min gradient at phi0 0.10 was slightly too steep, so test the same tG with the other 1.000-scoring phi0 value. This checks whether the higher starting composition preserves the critical separation better at faster slope and further maps robustness around the optimum.

With tG 12 min too steep, check the other side of the optimum at the winning phi window to define the full ridge of high performance. This will confirm whether 14 min is truly optimal or whether extra slope relief still preserves a maximum score in this narrowed window.

The optimum is established, so use the last two injections to refine the edge of the plateau around the second 1.000 method. Combining phi0 0.15 with the lower phi1 0.80 will test whether that branch stays at maximum score or falls off from added time penalty.

Use the final injection to complete the local map around the optimum by testing the one remaining adjacent combination of higher phi0 with higher phi1. This confirms the boundary of the 1.000-scoring plateau and whether either winning method has a broader robust neighborhood.
